newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen says telecoms unit not for sale.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen says telecoms unit not for sale.

text.p: Thyssen Telecom, the telecommunications arm of German steel group Thyssen AG, said on Tuesday telecoms was a core business of the group and that the unit it was not for sale.
Thyssen Telecom Hans-Erich Forster told a news briefing in Duesseldorf that Thyssen was determined to continue with its telecom business.

His comments follow speculation, denied by the Thyssen group itself on Monday, that it was looking to sell its 30 percent stake in the E-Plus Mobilfunk mobile telephony network, a major part of the Thyssen Telecom business.
Forster, managing director of the telecom unit, said that Thyssen Telecom had in recent discussions of the Thyssen group portfolio been put forward as a potential core business of the group.

Forster said Thyssen Telecom would in future organise its business into three areas, that of the E-Plus and DFR mobile units, its Plusnet fixed-wire service-provider, and its newly-created Multimedia-Service-Gesellschaft (MSG multimedia services.
He added that the business plan had been constructed in such a way that Thyssen could operate without other partners, although cooperations in specific projects were not ruled out, he said.
